key_insight: A-atom potentials can be derived exactly from linear ACE models and still recover key disordered-alloy properties, provided the chemical site basis is chosen carefully.
engineering_relevance: This enables more accurate, data-efficient alloy thermodynamics and property prediction for disordered materials using much smaller training sets than typical interatomic potential workflows.
method: Fit a linear ACE to Fe-W data from an EAM potential and compare the derived A-atom model against explicit random supercells.
Train a linear ACE on ~1500 small Mo-Nb DFT structures and derive A-atom potentials for benchmark properties.
Test elastic constants, lattice parameter, mixing enthalpy, Bain path, and surface energies across different chemical site bases.
evidence_signal: The paper reports agreement with disordered-phase properties from explicit supercells/EAM for Fe-W and with DFT elastic constants, lattice parameter, mixing enthalpy, Bain path, and—only for the occupation basis—surface energies for Mo-Nb.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on the chosen chemical site basis, and not all bases reproduce surface energetics even when bulk properties are captured.
paper_title: Benchmarking average atom potentials derived from atomic cluster expansions
